subject: Derivative outputs, model-improvement opt-out and KMS residency — HelixMed
messages:
From: Sarah Bennet <sarah.bennet@helixmed.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying derivative outputs and model-improvement opt-out (HelixMed)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked great. Before procurement starts the DPA redline, legal asked me to confirm two operational points so we can avoid a lengthy back-and-forth:

1) "Derivative outputs" language in your standard DPA vs. "service outputs" — we need a short plain-English description of what Redwood considers an output that can be licensed back to us vs. anything you would consider a derived model improvement. For our board and privacy team it matters whether inference results could ever be used to retrain or benchmark models.

2) KMS residency and cross-border routing — we want assurance that customer-provided KMS keys will stay in-region for key wrapping and that telemetry used for service health/metrics is not retained beyond 30 days in any non-US region without explicit consent.

Attached is a short checklist of items legal would like evidence for (redline coming from procurement later this week). Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to: no-model-training on HelixMed inputs; an affirmative definition of outputs we license back to customers; and the KMS residency constraints?

If helpful, loop in your security/ops folks; we can do a short call Friday (we're PT).

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Bennet
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
HelixMed

Attachment: HelixMed_no-train_evidence_request.xlsx (spreadsheet with requested proof items: SOC2 control references, KMS zone map, retention windows)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sarah Bennet <sarah.bennet@helixmed.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying derivative outputs and model-improvement opt-out (HelixMed)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Jonas (Security) and Connor (Infra/Operations) so they can confirm implementation details. High-level answers up front so procurement has context:

- No-training commitment: Redwood will agree to a contractual "no model training" commitment for HelixMed data processed under a no-train DPA addendum. Operationally we tag tenant interactions and ensure they are excluded from model-update pipelines and long-term training telemetry stores. We can provide an ops-runbook excerpt showing the tagging and exclusion steps.

- Outputs definition: By "service outputs" we mean the generated content returned to the customer in response to their API/chat requests (text, embeddings, re-ranks). "Derived models"/"model improvements" refer to any artifact (weights, fine-tuned checkpoints, evaluation datasets) used to update or benchmark Redwood models. For HelixMed, we can add a DPA clause that explicitly states HelixMed has exclusive rights to the service outputs and that Redwood will not create derivative models from HelixMed inputs.

- KMS residency & telemetry: We support customer-managed KMS (CloudKMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can pin key wrapping to a region. Connor — can you confirm which regions we can commit for key wrapping and whether we can provide an onshore-only telemetry retention configuration for this account?

If that sounds okay I can draft a short addendum (operational definitions + commitments) to attach to the DPA and share with your team. Would Friday at 11am PT for a short 30-minute call work for HelixMed?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | privacy@redwood.com

- A limited SLA exception for audit log exports to support our internal compliance audits (they want guaranteed export within 14 days).
- Evidence of the no-training operational toggle: procurement needs an example of the tagging and pipeline exclusion mechanism (we don't need full logs, just a sanitized runbook excerpt and a short diagram).

Redline attached. Can your security/ops folks review and tell procurement if they can accept or propose alternate language? We prefer to avoid a protracted security evidence process.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachment: HelixMed_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (PDF with track changes)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: HelixMed DPA redline — action items and proposed language

Jonas / Connor — summary and action list for HelixMed (they sent legal checklist + procurement redline):

Context:
- Enterprise prospect HelixMed requires a contractual "no model training" commitment plus operational evidence that tenant inputs are excluded from model updates and long-term telemetry used for training. They also want KMS key wrapping pinned to US regions and a 30-day cap on non-US telemetry retention unless expressly allowed.

Proposed draft text to add to the DPA (plain-English paragraph to include in an addendum):
"For HelixMed, Redwood will not use Customer Data to train or improve any of its models. Customer Data and Service Outputs shall remain the exclusive property and entitlement of Customer, and Redwood shall not (a) create derivative model artifacts, weights, or checkpoints from Customer Data, or (b) incorporate Customer Data into any model improvement, benchmarking, or internal evaluation datasets."

Operational evidence we need to provide to procurement/legal:
- Short runbook excerpt (sanitized) showing tenant request tagging and the exclusion step before model-update jobs (Connor)
- KMS residency confirmation and list of candidate regions we can guarantee for key wrapping (Connor)
- Security control reference mapping (SOC2 control ids + relevant internal docs) and a short note on telemetry retention windows (Jonas)
- A short diagram of the export path and SLA for audit export (14-day export commitment) — confirm if we can meet 14 days or propose 21 days with compensating controls.

Please reply with:
- Connor: regions we can commit to for key wrapping and feasibility of providing a sanitized runbook excerpt by EOD Wed. Also confirm whether the 14-day export SLA is operationally feasible.
- Jonas: controls mapping and suggested wording for telemetry retention (30 days non-US) and proof artifacts we can provide without exposing customer data.

I'll draft the addendum language after your replies and share with Sarah/Alex. If we can commit to the runbook excerpt + regions + a controls matrix, procurement should be able to finish the redline quickly.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
